FOREWORD

0.

0.1 This 1ndian"Standard ( First Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 September 1983, after the draft finalized by the Metallic Finishes Sectional Committee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council. 0.2 This standard has been formulated with a view to laying down in the country. requirements for copper anodes used by electroplaters Since impurities in copper anodes will have deleterious effect on the electroplating process, electrolytic copper has only been recommended for the making of these anodes. 0.3 In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been paid to the manufacturing and trade practices followed in the country in this field. 0.4 This standard is intended to cover the technical provisions relating to copper anodes for electroplating, and it does not include all the necessary provisions of a contract. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accorThe number of significant places retained in dance with IS : 2-1960*. the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

3. SHAPE 3.1 Copper

AND SIZE

anodes shall be supplied in either cast, rolled, or extruded form from electrolytic copper or cut to size from electrolytic cathode plates, as specified by the purchaser. Oval shape of anode is considered to be best from the point of view of even flow of current and uniformity of deposition. Dimensions of the anode shall be as agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 4. FREEDOM

FROM DEFECTS

4.1 Anodes

shall be clean, substantially free from cracks, warps, inclusions, porosity, ragged edges, surface films, such as rolling skin, and other defects which may adversely affect uniform dissolution while in use. 5. MARKING with the name, initials or trade-mark of the manufacturer. In case of anodes with hooks, the name, initials or trade-mark of the manufacturer shall be placed near the hooks.

A-3.1 From each of the anodes selected in accordance with A-2, drillings shall be obtained from not fewer than three widely-spaced positions. These drillings shall be obtained as specified in A-3.2 and drillings from each anode shall be stored separately. A-3.2 Select a sharpened twist drill ( 6 to 10 mm drill should be Thoroughly clean the drill in light petroleum and wipe clean suitable ). Free the anode from any loose impurity by means of a with muslin. Bore the holes to approximately 10 percent of the steel wire brush. thickness of the anode and discard the drillings therefrom. Place the anode on a clean tinned iron sheet and drill a further 80 percent of the thickness. Collect the drillings thus obtained and transfer to a clean If a larger quantity of drillings is required, more holes may container. be drilled as described above. Before analyzing, the drillings should be washed in light petroleum. A-4.
